items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: Guy Lombardo, he started in '28, Guy.

ctx.x: Yes, yes. Yes, but you know what I preferred? I preferred to play popular music. Because people seemed to like popular music. They danced better, they enjoyed it better, because they could sing and hum it. And the blues was just the blues. It's just different words and a different signature on top, that's all. But it was still the blues. So that's what it was.

And then, here the band started jumping up, too. The Dorsey Brothers and (inaudible) Benny Goodman, Guy Lombardo, he started in '28, Guy. Vincent Lopez, he started, too. And slowly but surely, each year a different band would show up. Well, they were colored bands that came to New York, too. And, of course, when they got here, I was here.

Well, you couldn't work with no more than one band at a time, because we belonged to Local 802. If you sign up for one band, you got to play with that band. You can't break your contract. But I could have played with a different band. But when I'm with one, I had to stay with one.
